newsitem.title: USA: Rapist of Clinton cousin paroled.
newsitem.headline: Rapist of Clinton cousin paroled.

text.p: An Arkansas prison inmate serving a life sentence for the rape of President Clinton's cousin will be paroled, officials said Thursday.

The inmate, Wayne Dumond, was convicted of kidnapping and raping Ashley Stephens, a distant cousin of President Clinton, in 1984. Stephens, who was 17 at the time of the assault, chose to identify herself in recent months as Dumond's victim to publicly fight Dumond's application for release.
"I'm in shock," said Stephens. "I'm really too upset to comment."

The case attracted national attention in its earliest days because Dumond was castrated in his east Arkansas home while awaiting trial for the rape, which occurred at Forrest City, Arkansas, about 95 miles east of Little Rock near the Tennessee border.
The local sheriff, since deceased, displayed Dumond's testicles in a jar of formaldahyde on his desk.

"I concur with the Board's action," said a statement from Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee, who created a political firestorm shortly after taking office last year when he said he was considering clemency for Dumond, who has consistently denied any knowledge of the crime. More than 200 women demonstrated on the steps of the Arkansas capitol against a reduction in Dumond's life sentence.

"I had prepared myself for the possibility that he might be free someday, even though deep down inside I didn't think it would happen," Stephens said. "I don't think Wayne Dumond is ready for parole."
Clinton was governor at the time of the rape. Clinton's successor, Jim Guy Tucker, reduced Dumond's sentence making his eligible for parole. Tucker was succeeded by Huckabee.
